Title: Attention is All You Need to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated into many applications (e.g., web agents) to perform more sophisticated tasks.However, LLM-empowered applications are vulnerable to Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks, where instructions are injected via untrustworthy external data sources.This paper presents RENNERVATE, a defense framework to detect and prevent IPI attacks.RENNERVATE leverages attention features to detect the covert injection at a fine-grained token level, enabling precise sanitization that neutralizes IPI attacks while maintaining LLM functionalities.Specifically, the tokenlevel detector is materialized with a 2-step attentive pooling mechanism, which aggregates attention heads and response tokens for IPI detection and sanitization.Moreover, we establish a fine-grained IPI dataset, FIPI, to be open-sourced to support further research.Extensive experiments verify that RENNERVATE outperforms 15 commercial and academic IPI defense methods, achieving high precision on 5 LLMs and 6 datasets.We also demonstrate that RENNERVATE is transferable to unseen attacks and robust against adaptive adversaries.
Major_Contribution_Result: RENNERVATE detects and sanitizes indirect prompt injection using token-level attention features via 2-step attentive pooling, without modifying the target LLM. The authors release FIPI (reported as 100k IPI instances covering 5 attack methods and 300 NLP tasks). Experiments claim outperformance versus 15 commercial/academic defenses across 5 LLMs and 6 datasets; sanitization reduces ASRs substantially (e.g., reductions of 85.80%/72.10%/84.90%/66.90%/60.60% on ChatGLM/Dolly/Falcon/LLaMA2/LLaMA3 in reported settings). Against one adaptive adversary, ASRs fall from ~93–99.5% undefended to 0–5% with RENNERVATE.
Research_Limitations_Challenges: Authors note: (1) unlike model-modification defenses, RENNERVATE needs attention weights (providers or local/open models; API users need provider support or a shadow LLM); (2) sanitization may not fully remove injected-task-specific content, causing utility loss on some tasks (e.g., grammar correction).
Critics: Strong empirical IPI detection/sanitization study with a large fine-grained dataset and many baselines. Dependence on internal attentions limits black-box API agents unless a shadow model is used, which changes the deployment threat model. Evaluation is largely NLP-task IPI rather than full tool-using agent trajectories, so transfer to agent workflows needs care.
